en: *Quanshan jing* (Sutra on Encouraging Goodness), one fascicle.

By imperial decree, the Left Chancellor Jia Huang was ordered to distribute this to all prefectures for the benefit of sentient beings. Every day, recite the name of Amitābha Buddha one thousand times;
cease evil and practice good with your mouth. This year has been exceptionally hot, and there are none [who have escaped].
While harvesting,
several members of the assembly fell ill and died;
the foremost was a virulent fever.
On the second day, they die of walking;
on the third, they die of red and white dysentery;
on the fourth, they die of bloodshot eyes.
The fifth person died from complications of childbirth;
the sixth died from dysentery;
the seventh died from wind-disorder.
I now exhort sentient beings to transcribe this sutra to escape calamities that would bring ruin to a single family;
by transcribing it, one’s six close relatives are saved.
Should one see this sutra and fail to transcribe it, the entire family will perish.
By passing through the side gate above, one may overcome this difficulty.
Those without merit cannot behold this sutra;
this sutra comes from the south.
On the eighth day of the first month, there was a clap of thunder and lightning.
In the sky appeared a young boy,
four years of age.
Furthermore, he saw an old man on the road.
[The old man] saw a serpent with a body ten thousand feet long and a human head and bird claws, and he called out to the old man, saying:
It is as if Mount Tai were to collapse;
even if one must encounter ten million women, or if one has a wish for ten thousand pieces of gold, or suffers from an illness that is difficult to cure—
those who transcribe this sutra shall be spared from these calamities.
Let those who do not believe simply observe this: on the first day of the fourth month, three households shall provide one ox, and five men shall share one wife;
monks and nuns shall go from door to door to recite this sutra and circulate the sublime mantras of the Sage.
If one performs exorcisms for wind and pestilence yet does not avoid calamity,
it is better to exhort others toward Amitābha Buddha so that they may soon witness a time of peace.
*Quanshan jing* (Sutra on Exhorting to Goodness), one fascicle.
